title: The Ultimate Catering Miracle and the Hard Truth
paragraphs: §Bread and Fish for All

After this, Jesus went across the Sea of Galilee (some call it Tiberias). A huge crowd followed him, drawn by the miracles they had seen him do among the sick. When he got to the other side, he climbed a hill and sat down with his disciples around him. It was nearly time for the Passover Feast, which the Jews kept every year.

When Jesus looked up and saw that a massive crowd had arrived, he said to Philip, "Where can we buy bread to feed all these people?" He said this to stretch Philip's faith—he already knew what he was going to do.
Philip answered, "Two hundred silver pieces wouldn't buy enough bread for each person to get even a bite."
One of the disciples—it was Andrew, Simon Peter's brother—said, "There's a little boy here who has five barley loaves and two fish. But that's a drop in the bucket for a crowd like this."

Jesus said, "Make everyone sit down." There was a nice carpet of green grass there. They sat down—about five thousand of them. Then Jesus took the bread, gave thanks, and gave it to those who were seated. He did the same with the fish. Everyone ate as much as they wanted.
When they had eaten their fill, he told his disciples, "Gather the leftovers so nothing goes to waste." They got to work and filled twelve large baskets with leftovers from the five barley loaves.

The people realized God was at work among them in what Jesus had just done. They said, "This is the Prophet for sure—God's Prophet, right here in Galilee!" Jesus saw that in their excitement they were about to grab him and force him to be king, so he slipped away back up the mountain by himself.

In the evening his disciples went down to the sea, got into a boat, and headed back across the water to Capernaum. It had grown quite dark and Jesus still hadn't come back. A huge wind blew up, churning the sea. They were maybe three or four miles out when they saw Jesus walking on the sea, quite close to the boat. They were scared out of their minds, but he reassured them: "It's me. It's all right. Don't be afraid." So they took him on board, and in no time they reached land—the exact spot they were headed to.

The next day, the crowd that had stayed behind realized there had been only one boat, and that Jesus had not gotten into it with his disciples—they had seen them leave without him. By now boats from Tiberias had pulled up near where they had eaten the bread the Master had blessed. So when the crowd realized he was gone and wasn't coming back, they piled into the Tiberias boats and headed for Capernaum, looking for Jesus.
When they found him on the other side of the sea, they said, "Rabbi, when did you get here?"
Jesus answered, "You've come looking for me not because you saw God in what I did, but because I fed you, filled your stomachs—and for free.

"Don't waste your energy chasing food that goes bad. Work for the food that sticks with you, food that nourishes your lasting life—food the Son of Man provides. He and what he does are guaranteed by God the Father to last."
§The Bread of Life
To that they said, "Well, what do we have to do to get in on God's work?"
Jesus said, "Sign on with the One God has sent. That kind of commitment gets you in on God's work."

They waffled: "Why don't you give us a clue about who you are—just a hint of what's going on? When we see what's up, we'll commit. Show us what you can do. Moses fed our ancestors with bread in the desert. The Scriptures say: 'He gave them bread from heaven to eat.'"

Jesus responded, "The real point of that Scripture isn't that Moses gave you bread from heaven—it's that my Father is right now offering you bread from heaven, the real bread. The Bread of God came down out of heaven and is giving life to the world."
They jumped at that: "Master, give us this bread, now and forever!"

Jesus said, "I am the Bread of Life. The person who aligns with me will never hunger and never thirst, ever. I've told you this straight, because even though you've seen me in action, you don't really believe me. Everyone the Father gives me eventually comes running to me. And once that person is with me, I hold on and don't let go. I came down from heaven not to follow my own agenda but to do the will of the One who sent me.

"This, in a nutshell, is that will: everything the Father handed over to me gets completed—not a single detail missed—and at the wrap-up of time I have everything and everyone put together, whole and upright. This is what my Father wants: anyone who sees the Son and trusts who he is and what he does, and aligns with him, will enter real life, eternal life. My part is to put them on their feet, alive and whole, at the completion of time."

At this, because he said, "I am the Bread that came down from heaven," the Jews started arguing about him: "Isn't this Joseph's son? Don't we know his father? Don't we know his mother? How can he say, 'I came down out of heaven,' and expect anyone to believe him?"

Jesus said, "Don't bicker about me among yourselves. You're not in charge here—the Father who sent me is in charge. He draws people to me; that's the only way you'll ever come. Only then do I do my work: putting people together, setting them on their feet, ready for the End. This is what the prophets meant when they wrote, 'And then they will all be personally taught by God.' Anyone who has spent any time listening to the Father—really listening, and therefore learning—comes to me to be taught personally. To see it with his own eyes, hear it with his own ears, from me, since I got it firsthand from the Father. No one has seen the Father except the One who shares being with the Father—and you can see me.

"I'm telling you the most solemn truth: Whoever believes in me has real, eternal life. I am the Bread of Life. Your ancestors ate the manna in the desert and died. But here is Bread that truly comes down out of heaven. Anyone who eats this Bread will never die. I am the Bread—living Bread!—who came down out of heaven. Anyone who eats this Bread will live, and forever! The Bread I present to the world, so it can eat and live, is myself—this flesh-and-blood self."
At this, the Jews started fighting among themselves: "How can this man serve up his flesh as a meal?"

But Jesus didn't back down an inch. "Only as you eat and drink flesh and blood—the flesh and blood of the Son of Man—do you have life in you. The one who brings a hearty appetite to this eating and drinking has eternal life and will be fit and ready for the Final Day. My flesh is real food and my blood is real drink. By eating my flesh and drinking my blood, you enter into me and I into you. Just as the fully alive Father sent me and I live because of him, so the one who makes a meal of me lives because of me. This is the Bread from heaven. Your ancestors ate bread and later died. Whoever eats this Bread will live forever."
He said these things while teaching in the meeting place in Capernaum.
§Too Tough to Swallow
Many of his disciples heard this and said, "This is tough teaching—too tough to swallow."

Jesus sensed his disciples were struggling with this and said, "Does this completely rattle you? What would happen if you saw the Son of Man going up to where he came from? The Spirit is what gives life. Sheer muscle and willpower don't make anything happen. Every word I've spoken to you is a Spirit-word, and so it creates life. But some of you are resisting, refusing to have any part in this." (Jesus knew from the start who wasn't going to risk themselves with him. He also knew who would betray him.) He went on: "This is why I told you earlier that no one can come to me on his own. You get to me only as a gift from the Father."
After this, many of his disciples left. They didn't want to be associated with him anymore. Then Jesus gave the Twelve their chance: "Do you want to leave too?"
Peter replied, "Master, who would we go to? You have the words of real, eternal life. We've already committed ourselves, confident that you are the Holy One of God."

Jesus responded, "Haven't I handpicked you, the Twelve? Yet one of you is a devil!" He was talking about Judas, son of Simon Iscariot. This man—one of the Twelve!—was already getting ready to betray him.
